rowLaw is the countable dependent product of uniform measures on Fin(j+1). The projection to coordinate j therefore has exactly that uniform law, including j=0 where Fin 1 is a singleton. This supports arbitrary positive remaining-set cardinality through coordinate cardinality-1; no hidden upper bound by the component count is imposed. The proof remains unfilled. For each k, partition a history-measurable event E by the countably many possible remaining finite sets A. On the piece remaining=A, history independence of the whole fresh row makes its coordinate card(A)-1 uniform and independent of that piece. Sorting A is a bijection from Fin(card A) to its distinct occurrences, so the probability of selecting j is 1/card A when j belongs to A and zero otherwise. Summing these eventwise identities is exactly FreshAssignments. If A is empty, both guarded integrands vanish and getD 0 causes no spurious selected event. Measurability follows from the countable finite-set partition and coordinate evaluations. The compiled type explicitly uses history k for remaining and the ambient sigma algebra for rows and Indep; hhistory is an actual sub-sigma-algebra premise. This lemma is conditional on row/history independence and does not assert it for a particular execution without proof. The proof remains unfilled.
